pages.text: A cold desert under a butterscotch sky. The air is thin carbon dioxide at under one hundredth of Earth's pressure, gravity is 0.38 g and nights fall far below freezing. You need a sealed suit here, not just oxygen.
The north is a low, smooth plain; the south is old cratered highland. Look for the great volcanoes, the long rift canyons, dune seas and the polar ice caps.
Storms can wrap the whole planet for days. They dim the sun, so solar panels give much less power, and they hide everything beyond a few blocks. Dust-proof seals keep your machines and suit running.
The fine dust scatters red light to the sides but lets blue light pass straight on, so around a low sun the sky turns blue: the opposite of Earth.
